to pierce, thrust, or punch through
la:verb:percutio.html:
per-cŭtĭo, cussi, cussum, 3 (
perf. contr. percusti for percussisti, ), v. a.
quatio
.
(With the notion of the per predominating.) To strike through and through, to thrust or pierce through (syn.: percello, transfigo).
Lit.: percussus cultello,: gladio percussus,: Mamilio pectus percussum,: coxam Aeneae,: vena percutitur,a vein is opened, blood is let,: fossam,to cut through, dig a trench,; .—
Transf., to slay, kill (class.; cf.: neco, perimo, ico, ferio): aliquem securi,to behead,; : collum percussa securi Victima,; : aliquem veneno,: hostem,; .—Hence, percutere foedus, to make a league, conclude a treaty (because an animal was slaughtered on the occasion; only post-Aug. for ferio, ico), Auct. B. Alex. 44: cum Albanis foedus percussit,; ; .—
(With the idea of the verb predominating.) To strike, beat, hit, smite, shoot, etc. (cf.: ico, pulso, ferio).
Lit.
In gen. (class.): ceu lapidem si Percutiat lapis aut ferrum,: cum Cato percussus esset ab eo, qui arcam ferebat,had been struck,: januam manu,; : turres de caelo percussae,struck with lightning,; cf.: hunc nec Juppiter fulmine percussit,: percussus ab aspide calcatā,stung, bitten,; cf.: PERCVSSVS A VIPERA, Inscr. Vermigl. Iscriz. Perug. p. 319; ; : color percussus luce refulgit,struck,; cf. ; : auriculae (voce) percussae,: percussus vocibus circus,.—Neutr.: sol percussit super caput,.—
In partic.
To strike, stamp, coin money (post-Aug.): ut nummum argenteum notā sideris Capricorni percusserit,; . —
To strike, play a musical instrument (poet.): lyram,; .—
As t. t. in weaving, to throw the shuttle with the woof: (lacernae) male percussae textoris pectine Galli, badly or coarsely woven, .—
Haec meraclo se percussit flore Libyco (=vino Mareotico), to get drunk, (cf.: sauciare se flore Liberi, Enn. ap. ).—
Trop.
To smite, strike, visit with calamity of any kind (class.): percussus calamitate,: percussus fortunae vulnere,: ruina,: anathemate. : plaga,: in stuporem,.—
To strike, shock, make an impression upon, affect deeply, move, astound (class.): percussisti me de oratione prolatā,; : audivi ex Gavio, Romae esse hominem, et fuisse assiduum: percussit animum, it struck me, made me suspicious, , b, 3: animos probabilitate,: percussus atrocissimis litteris,: fragor aurem percutit,.—
To cheat, deceive, impose upon one (class.): aliquem probe,: hominem eruditum,: hominem strategemate,: aliquem palpo,to flatter,.—
(Acc. to II. A. 2. a.) To strike, stamp (post-Aug.): facta dictaque tua unā formā percussa sunt,.

la:verb:percipio.html:
per-cĭpĭo, cēpi, ceptum, 3 (old form of the
pluperf. percepset for percepisset, Poët. ap. ; v. Trag. Rel. p. 207 Rib.), v. a.
capio
, to take wholly, to seize entirely (cf. occupo).
Lit.
To take possession of, to seize, occupy: mihi horror misero membra percipit dictis tuis,: priusquam percipit (eum) insania,; : neque urbis odium me umquam percipit,: vitae percipit humanos odium,; .—
To take to one's self, to assume: varii sensus animantibus insunt, quorum quisque suam proprie rem percipit in se,: rigorem,: colorem,: sucum thymi,.—
To get, obtain, receive: serere, percipere, condere fructus,to gather, collect,: praemia,: fructum ex oleā,: civitatem ab aliquo,: hereditatem,; .—
Trop. (so most freq. in class. lang.; syn.: sentio, intellego, comprehendo).
To perceive, observe: ne, quod hic agimus, erus percipiat fieri,: quod neque oculis, neque auribus, neque ullo sensu percipi potest,: crebraeque nunc querelae, nunc minae percipiebantur,were heard,; : quae dicam,i. e. hear,: et aures, cum sonum percipere debeant,; so, percipe auribus,hear, give ear, et saep.—
To feel: neque majorem voluptatem ex infinito tempore aetatis percipi posse, quam ex hoc percipiatur,: voluptatem,: luctus,: dolores,: gaudia,.—
To learn,

know, conceive, comprehend, understand, perceive, etc.: res percepta et cognita,: percipere et comprehendere,: cognosci et percipi posse,: aliquid animo,: artificium aliquod,: virtutem et humanitatem,: philosophiam,: praecepta artis,: omnium civium nomina perceperat,knew,: nomen Graecum, sed perceptum usu a nostris,known,.—Hence, perceptus, a, um, P. a., perceived, observed.—Hence, subst.: percep-ta, ōrum, n., doctrines, principles, rules of an art or science: percepta appello, quae dicuntur Graecis θεωρήματα, . —Sing.: pro percepto liquere,as proved, certain,.

la:verb:percello.html:
per-cello, cŭli, culsum, 3 (perculsi for perculi, ; ), v. a.
cf.: procella, celer
,
to beat down, throw down; to overturn, upset (class.; syn.: percutio, deicio).
Lit.: ventus Cercius plaustrum oneratum percellit, Cato ap. ; cf.: vento perculsam ratem, Afran. ap. Müll. (Com. Rel. p. 154 fin. Rib.): magnas quercus, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 194 Vahl.): abietem, Varr. ap. : alii adnutat ... alii percellit pedem, Naev. ap. (Com. Rel. p. 17 Rib.): perii! perculit me prope,; : radicibus arborum,: Mars communis saepe spoliantem jam et exsultantem evertit et perculit ab abjecto,: eos Martis vis perculit,.—Prov.: Perii, plaustrum perculi! I've upset my cart, i. e. I've done for myself, .—
Transf., to strike, smite, hit: fetiali Postumius genu femur perculit,; cf. : aliquem cuspide,; .— Poet.: vox repens perculit urbem,struck, reached,.—
Trop.
To cast down, overthrow, ruin, destroy: adulescentiam perculisse atque afflixisse,; ; : rem publicam,: aliquem,.—
To strike with consternation, to deject, daunt, dispirit, discourage, dishearten: haec te vox non perculit? non perturbavit?: timore perculsi membra,: civitates atrocibus edictis,; : animos (timor),.—
To urge on, excite, impel: volucres perculsae corda tuā vi,: aliquem ad turpitudinem,.—Perf.: perculit, in a neutr. signif., for perculsus est,.

la:verb:percurro.gloss: to run, hasten or pass through, traverse, pass or run over or along; stroke
senses: to run, hasten or pass through, traverse, pass or run over or along; stroke
la:verb:percurro.html:
per-curro, percŭcurri or percurri, percursum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act., to run through, hasten through; to pass through, traverse, run over, pass over or along class.; syn. peragro).
Lit.: percurrere agrum Picenum,: labro calamos,: rapido percurrens turbine campos,: pollice chordas,: conventus,: Tenchteros et Cattos,: aristas,to speed over,: percurrens luna fenestras,: pectine telas,; : ignea rima micans percurrit lumine nimbos,: tempora nodo, i. e. to wind or bind round, .—Pass., : hortus fontano umore percurritur,.—
Trop., to run through: amplissimos honores percucurrit,i. e. filled the highest offices one after another,: quaesturam, praeturam,; .—In pass.: percursis honorum gradibus,.—
To run over in speaking, to mention cursorily: partes, quas modo percucurri,: quae breviter a te percursa sunt,: multas res oratione,: omnia poenarum nomina,: celebres in eā arte quam maximā brevitate,: modice beneficia,to mention in a cursory manner,: paucis, quae cujusque ductu gens,; .—
To run over in the mind or with the eye, to scan briefly, to look over: multa animo et cogitatione, multa etiam legendo,: atque id percurram brevi,: oculo,to run over,: paginas in annalious magistratuum,to run through, to look over,: pugnas,.—Impers. pass., .—
Of feelings, sensations, to run through, penetrate, agitate: omnium pectora occulto metu percurrente,. —
Neutr., to run, run along to or over any thing (class.): curriculo percurre (ad villam),run thither quickly,: ad forum,: ad aliquem, Cael. ap. : per temonem (currūs),to run along the pole,: per mare et terras,.—
Trop. (very rare), to pass; with per, to run over in speaking, touch upon in succession: nam per omnis civitates quae decumas habent, percurrit oratio mea,.
